subproblem.title: Hole estimate (10') for graph points off spt V (corrected Simon 2.6 (9)-(10))
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l >= 0 and p > n there are delta_2 > 0, eps_2 > 0 and C_2 > 0, depending only on n, l, p, such that: if U is open, V = v(M, theta) is a RectifiableVarifold n l U with generalized mean curvature H in U, 0 < delta <= delta_2 and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold, q is a linear isometry of R^(n+l) with T_0 := rotatedPlane q and P := its orthogonal projection, f : R^n -> R^l is eps-Lipschitz on R^n with 0 <= eps <= eps_2, Fhat := q(graphOver f R^n), and zeta in Fhat satisfies |zeta| <= 2 delta rho and 0 < d := dist(zeta, spt V) <= delta rho (infDist to V.support), then there is y in spt V with |y - zeta| = d, and, with s := d/2, s^n <= C_2 [ mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + integral over B_{3s}(zeta) of |p_x - P|^2 dmu(x) ], where mu = V.weight, p_x = V.tangentProj x, |.| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNormSq), the ball measure is taken as a real number (toReal) and the integral is the Bochner integral.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ δ₂ ε₂ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < δ₂ ∧ 0 < ε₂ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δ₂ → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ ε₂ → LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal ε) f → ∀ ζ ∈ q '' graphOver f univ, ‖ζ‖ ≤ 2 * (δ * ρ) → 0 < infDist ζ V.support → infDist ζ V.support ≤ δ * ρ → ∃ y ∈ V.support, dist y ζ = infDist ζ V.support ∧ (infDist ζ V.support / 2) ^ n ≤ C₂ * ((V.weight (closedBall ζ (3 * (infDist ζ V.support / 2)) \ q '' graphOver f univ)).toReal + ∫ x in closedBall ζ (3 * (infDist ζ V.support / 2)), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection) ∂V.weight)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof, i.e. the corrected form (10') of Simon 2.6 (9)-(10): the annulus is B_{3s} \ B_s, the monotonicity constants are the corrected ones (Lambda = 4 p delta/(p-n)), and the closest point y is produced explicitly.

Notation. (The constants delta_2, eps_2, C_2 of this lemma are its own; they are unrelated to the internal constant C_2 used in the proof of the sibling height_cone.) mu := V.weight; spt V := V.support = U ∩ spt mu; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; Q := I - P, so |Q v| = dist(v, T_0); p_x^perp v := v - p_x v; tilt(A) := integral over A of |p_x - P|^2 dmu; ||A|| <= |A| (operator norm vs Hilbert-Schmidt norm).

Inputs.
(D) [sibling child density_monotonicity] delta_0 in (0, 1/8] and C_0 >= 0 such that for 0 < delta <= delta_0 and 2.3: (i) mu(B_t(w)) <= 2 omega_n t^n for |w| <= 3 delta rho, 0 < t <= rho/2; (ii) mu(B_t(w)) >= omega_n t^n/2 for w in spt V, |w| <= 3 delta rho, 0 < t <= rho/2; (iii) for |w| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < t <= r <= rho/2: r^-n mu(B_r(w)) <= e^2 t^-n mu(B_t(w)) + C_0 delta + e^2 * (integral over B_r(w) \ B_t(w) of |p_x^perp(x - w)|^2 |x - w|^(-n-2) dmu).
(F1) [sibling child tangent_plane_ae] x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; every p_x is an orthogonal projection or 0, so ||p_x|| <= 1 and |p_x^perp v| <= |v|. Hence all integrands below are bounded on the relevant balls and mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and the balls (contained in B_rho(0)) have finite mu-measure, so every Bochner integral below is a genuine finite integral, and integrals of nonnegative functions are monotone in the domain and in the integrand.
(F2) spt mu is closed, mu(R^(n+l) \ spt mu) = 0, spt V = U ∩ spt mu, and 0 in spt V (2.3).

1. Constants. A_8 := 72 * 3^n e^2/omega_n; delta_2 := min{delta_0, 3^-n omega_n/(4 (C_0 + 1))} > 0; eps_2 := (4 A_8 omega_n 5^n)^(-1/2) > 0; C_2 := 2 A_8 > 0. Let 0 < delta <= delta_2 and the remaining hypotheses hold; note delta <= 1/8 and C_0 delta <= 3^-n omega_n/4.
2. Closest point (parent 5(a)). spt mu is closed and nonempty (0 in spt V ⊆ spt mu), so there is y in spt mu with |y - zeta| = dist(zeta, spt mu) <= dist(zeta, spt V) = d (spt V ⊆ spt mu). Then |y| <= |zeta| + d <= 3 delta rho < rho, so y in B_rho(0) ⊆ U, hence y in U ∩ spt mu = spt V and |y - zeta| >= d. Thus |y - zeta| = d = dist(zeta, spt mu): no point of spt mu lies in the open ball of radius d about zeta. Put s := d/2 > 0. As B_s(zeta) is contained in that open ball, mu(B_s(zeta)) <= mu(R^(n+l) \ spt mu) = 0. Also |zeta| <= 2 delta rho <= 3 delta rho, |y| <= 3 delta rho, s <= delta rho/2, 3s <= 3 delta rho/2 <= rho/2 and 5s <= 5 delta rho/2 <= rho/2 (delta <= 1/8), and B_{5s}(y) ⊆ B_rho(0).
3. Monotonicity at zeta (parent 5(b)). By (D)(iii) at w = zeta with t = s and r = 3s: (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= e^2 * 0 + C_0 delta + e^2 J, J := integral over B_{3s}(zeta) \ B_s(zeta) of |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 |x - zeta|^(-n-2) dmu. On that annulus |x - zeta| > s, so J <= s^(-n-2) I, where I := integral over B_{3s}(zeta) of |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 dmu (nonnegative integrand, larger domain). Hence (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= C_0 delta + e^2 s^(-n-2) I.
4. Lower bound (parent 5(c)). B_s(y) ⊆ B_{3s}(zeta) because |y - zeta| = 2s, so by (D)(ii) at y (y in spt V, |y| <= 3 delta rho, s <= rho/2): (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) >= (3s)^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= 3^-n omega_n/2. Since C_0 delta <= 3^-n omega_n/4, step 3 gives 3^-n omega_n/4 <= e^2 s^(-n-2) I, i.e. s^(n+2) <= 4 * 3^n e^2 omega_n^-1 I.
5. Upper bound for I (parent 5(d)). For x in B_{3s}(zeta), p_x^perp = Q + (P - p_x), so |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 <= 2 |Q(x - zeta)|^2 + 2 ||P - p_x||^2 |x - zeta|^2 <= 2 |Q(x - zeta)|^2 + 18 s^2 |p_x - P|^2. If x in Fhat, write x = q(graphPoint u (f u)) and zeta = q(graphPoint v (f v)); then x - zeta = q(graphPoint (u - v) 0) + q(graphPoint 0 (f u - f v)), where the first vector lies in T_0 and the second is orthogonal to T_0 (q preserves orthogonality), so |Q(x - zeta)| = |f(u) - f(v)| <= eps |u - v| <= eps |x - zeta| <= 3 eps s. If x is not in Fhat, |Q(x - zeta)| <= |x - zeta| <= 3s. Since B_{3s}(zeta) ⊆ B_{5s}(y), (D)(i) at y gives mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= mu(B_{5s}(y)) <= 2 omega_n 5^n s^n. Fhat is closed (f is continuous and q is a homeomorphism, so the graph and its image are closed), hence Borel, and therefore
 I <= 18 eps^2 s^2 mu(B_{3s}(zeta) ∩ Fhat) + 18 s^2 mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + 18 s^2 tilt(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= 18 s^2 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))].
6. Conclusion (parent 5(e)). Combining steps 4 and 5 and dividing by s^2 > 0: s^n <= A_8 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))]. Since eps^2 <= eps_2^2 = 1/(4 A_8 omega_n 5^n), the first term is at most s^n/2; absorbing it gives s^n <= 2 A_8 [mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))] = C_2 [...]. Together with y from step 2 (y in spt V, |y - zeta| = d = dist(zeta, spt V)) this is the claim, with mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) finite (the set lies in B_rho(0)) and therefore equal to its real value. QED
proof_key_steps: Constants A_8 = 72 * 3^n e^2/omega_n, delta_2 = min{delta_0, 3^-n omega_n/(4(C_0+1))}, eps_2 = (4 A_8 omega_n 5^n)^(-1/2), C_2 = 2 A_8
Closest point: y in spt V with |y - zeta| = d = dist(zeta, spt mu); hence mu(B_{d/2}(zeta)) = 0
Annular monotonicity (D)(iii) at zeta with radii s, 3s: (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= C_0 delta + e^2 s^(-n-2) I
Lower density at y and C_0 delta <= 3^-n omega_n/4 give s^(n+2) <= 4 * 3^n e^2 omega_n^-1 I
Split p_x^perp = Q + (P - p_x); graph cone bound |Q(x - zeta)| <= 3 eps s on Fhat and upper density at y give I <= 18 s^2 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_{3s}(zeta) minus Fhat) + tilt]
Absorb the eps^2 term using eps <= eps_2 to get s^n <= C_2 [mu(B_{3s}(zeta) minus Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))]

audit.reason: The hypotheses and conclusion match the frozen proposition. The closest point in the ambient measure support lies in U, hence in V.support. All required balls lie within the density estimates' range. Annular monotonicity, lower mass, graph slope and tilt bounds give the displayed inequality, with both absorption conditions verified. The parent's path argument supplies an admissible hole point; uniform tilt then contradicts this estimate and establishes the required reverse inclusion.
